iOS shows no pointer cursor; cursor values are ignored there.

Marked partial at the floor (full from Chrome 144 and Firefox 150, partial in every Safari); the carousel's row writes contain only so that a swipe at the row's end does not carry on to the page as a back swipe, and the row scrolls and snaps the same without it.
Mobile browsers show no resize handle on text areas; the declaration is ignored there.
iOS keeps the system selection colors; the rule is ignored there.
Text size adjustment exists only in mobile browsers; desktop Firefox and Safari ignore it, and the -webkit- form beside it covers Safari on iOS and Firefox on Android.
Chrome for Android, and Safari before 26.2, do not keep a minimum contrast for controls in the accent color; the library's accent passes 4.5:1 in both themes on its own.

Invoker commands are an enhancement below Chrome 135, Firefox 144 and Safari 26.2: js/commands.js stands in there - a popover command becomes the browser's own popovertarget inside the click, a dialog command calls showModal(), close() or requestClose(), a custom command dispatches the command event.

Partial at the floor only in its initial value (auto, none or implicit by version); the library always writes position-anchor out, and its value auto is supported where anchors are.
Partial in Chrome 129-143 only as a single keyword or beside span-all, where the anchored box may overflow the viewport; the library always pairs it with a span-inline-* keyword.

closedby is an enhancement below Chrome 134 and Firefox 141 and in Safari: js/dialog.js stands in there - a click on the backdrop of a modal dialog with closedby="any" asks it to close; Escape closes a modal dialog in every engine.

Below Chrome 144 and Firefox 150, and in Safari, the property does nothing on a scroll container that does not overflow; the library sets it only on lists that scroll when they are long, so that their end does not scroll the page.
An enhancement in Safari 18.0-18.1, which keep no gutter while a modal dialog locks the page's scroll; Safari's overlay scrollbars take no room, so nothing moves there.
An enhancement in Safari 18.0-18.1, which show the scrollbar under a scrolling tab strip; the strip still scrolls, and Safari's overlay scrollbars show only while scrolling.
Firefox matches :autofill only on autofilled user name and password fields; other autofilled fields show the browser's own autofill style instead of ours.
Desktop browsers have no viewport to set; the tag is for mobile browsers, where it is supported.

allow.name: selector:-webkit-search-decoration
allow.reason: Not in browser-compat-data: the decoration of search fields in WebKit and Blink, removed by the reset in a rule of its own, which Firefox ignores.

allow.name: selector:-webkit-outer-spin-button
allow.reason: Not in browser-compat-data: the outer spin button of number fields in WebKit and Blink; it shares its rule only with ::-webkit-inner-spin-button, so Firefox drops just that rule.

Below Firefox 148 and Safari 26.2 hidden="until-found" is a plain hidden: a region closed by --toggle stays closed until its button opens it, and only find in page cannot reach it there; where it is supported, find in page opens it.

allow.name: selector:-webkit-details-marker
allow.reason: Not in browser-compat-data: the triangle WebKit draws on a summary even with list-style: none (Safari before 18.4); the accordion hides it in a rule of its own, which Chrome and Firefox ignore.

allow.name: selector:-moz-meter-bar
allow.reason: Not in browser-compat-data: the value bar of a meter in Firefox; every rule that names it names no other engine's part, so Chrome and Safari drop just those rules and paint the meter by their ::-webkit-meter-* rules.

allow.name: selector:-moz-meter-sub-optimum
allow.reason: Not in browser-compat-data: Firefox's state of a meter whose value lies in the region next to the optimum; in rules of its own, as ::-moz-meter-bar.

allow.name: selector:-moz-meter-sub-sub-optimum
allow.reason: Not in browser-compat-data: Firefox's state of a meter whose value lies in the region farthest from the optimum; in rules of its own, as ::-moz-meter-bar.

repairs.reason: Engines that have anchors yet do not put a menu beside its button: Chrome 130-132 make no implicit anchor of a popover's invoker (api.HTMLButtonElement.popoverTargetElement.implicit_anchor_reference, from 133), Chrome 135-136 anchor a menu in a middle- or bottom-aligned table cell at the cell's top, and Safari 26 keeps a fixed menu below its button at the bottom of a page taller than the viewport - it judges the fallbacks by the page's scrollable area (WebKit bug 289743; measured in 26.4 and 26.5, fixed by 27.2). The guard measures each opened menu and places it itself there.
